title: Deep muscles of the gluteal region (posterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Outer surface of the ilium between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines.
Anterior surface of the greater trochanter of the femur.
Abducts and medially rotates the thigh. With gluteus medius it keeps the pelvis level in walking.
Upper border of the greater trochanter of the femur.
Laterally rotates the extended thigh and abducts the flexed thigh. Steadies the head of the femur in the acetabulum.
hy: It leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen and is the landmark of the gluteal region. The superior gluteal nerve and vessels emerge above it. The sciatic nerve, the inferior gluteal nerve and vessels and the pudendal nerve emerge below it.
The muscle can press on the sciatic nerve and cause pain in the buttock that runs down the back of the thigh (piriformis syndrome).

rows: Medial surface of the greater trochanter of the femur, with the tendon of obturator internus.
Laterally rotates the extended thigh and abducts the flexed thigh.
Inner surface of the obturator membrane and the bone around the obturator foramen.
Medial surface of the greater trochanter of the femur. Its tendon leaves the pelvis through the lesser sciatic foramen and turns sharply around the lesser sciatic notch.
Laterally rotates the extended thigh and abducts the flexed thigh.
hy: When an inflamed appendix lies in the pelvis against this muscle, turning the flexed hip inward hurts (obturator sign).

rows: Medial surface of the greater trochanter of the femur, with the tendon of obturator internus.
Laterally rotates the extended thigh and abducts the flexed thigh.
Lateral border of the ischial tuberosity.
Quadrate tubercle on the intertrochanteric crest of the femur.
Outer surface of the obturator membrane and the bone around the obturator foramen.
Posterior ilium, lateral sacrum and coccyx to the ischial tuberosity.
With the sacrospinous ligament it turns the sciatic notches into foramina and resists upward tilting of the lower sacrum under the weight of the trunk.
Lateral margin of the sacrum and coccyx to the ischial spine.
Turns the greater sciatic notch into the greater sciatic foramen and separates it from the lesser sciatic foramen. It resists upward tilting of the lower sacrum.
hy: The pudendal nerve leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, hooks around the ischial spine and this ligament, and enters the perineum through the lesser sciatic foramen.
